group.passage:
In November 1935, a fire at a house on Wimpole Street in London killed five women. The tragedy exposed a weakness in the city’s telephone system: operators at the exchange had no quick way of telling an emergency call from an ordinary one. A committee set up to study the problem called for a single number that would be easy to remember and free to dial from a public telephone box. On 30 June 1937, the number 999 came into service within 12 miles of Oxford Circus, and 1,336 calls were made to it in its first week. After the Second World War it spread to other large cities, and by 1976 it covered the whole country.
The United States waited three decades longer. Americans in trouble usually dialed 0 for an operator or looked up a seven-digit number for their local police or fire station. After a presidential commission recommended a single number in 1967, the telephone company AT&T announced in January 1968 that 911 would serve the whole country. Three digits, it reasoned, would be far easier to remember than seven. The first 911 call was made on 16 February 1968 in Haleyville, Alabama, yet the number spread slowly: by 1987, only half of all Americans could use it.
Europe faced a different problem. As more people traveled across borders, a visitor in danger might not know which number to call. In 1991, the countries of what is now the European Union agreed on 112 as a number that would work in every member state, and today it can be dialed free from both fixed and mobile phones. It usually exists alongside older national numbers, although a few countries, including Sweden and the Netherlands, have made it their only one.
Not every country uses one number for everything, as the table below shows. In Taiwan, as in Japan, 119 brings firefighters or an ambulance, while 110 reaches the police. Taiwan also accepts 112 from mobile phones, which can dial it even without a SIM card. A recorded message then asks the caller to press 0 for the police or 9 for fire and ambulance services, so when the signal is good, it is quicker to call 110 or 119 directly.

questions.stem: What do the stories of 999, 911, and 112 in the passage have in common?

options.A: Each number was introduced soon after a deadly fire in a big city.
options.B: Each number quickly replaced every other emergency number in its area.
options.C: Each number was first tried out in a small town before spreading.
options.D: Each made getting help simpler by offering a single, easy number.

translation_zh.text:
1935 年 11 月，倫敦溫波街一棟房子發生火災，五名女性喪生。這場悲劇暴露了這座城市電話系統的一個弱點：交換局的接線生沒有辦法快速分辨緊急電話和一般電話。為研究這個問題而成立的委員會，主張設立一個好記、而且能在公用電話亭免費撥打的單一號碼。1937 年 6 月 30 日，999 開始在牛津圓環周圍 12 英里內提供服務，第一週就有 1,336 通來電。第二次世界大戰後，它擴展到其他大城市，到了 1976 年已涵蓋全國。
美國晚了三十年。遇到麻煩的美國人通常撥 0 找接線生，或查出當地警察局、消防隊的七位數電話。1967 年一個總統委員會建議設立單一號碼後，電話公司 AT&T 在 1968 年 1 月宣布以 911 服務全國。它認為三個數字比七個數字好記得多。第一通 911 電話在 1968 年 2 月 16 日於阿拉巴馬州海利維爾撥出，但這個號碼普及得很慢：到了 1987 年，只有一半的美國人能使用。
歐洲面臨的是另一個問題。隨著越來越多人跨國旅行，遇到危險的旅客可能不知道該撥哪個號碼。1991 年，今日歐盟的各國同意以 112 作為在每個會員國都能使用的號碼；如今市內電話和手機都能免費撥打。它通常與各國原有的號碼並存，不過包括瑞典和荷蘭在內的少數國家，已把它當作唯一的緊急號碼。
如下表所示，並不是每個國家都用一個號碼處理所有事情。在台灣，和日本一樣，撥 119 會派來消防員或救護車，撥 110 則接通警察。台灣的手機也能撥 112，即使沒有 SIM 卡也可以。接通後語音會請來電者按 0 轉接警察，或按 9 轉接消防與救護；所以收訊良好時，直接撥 110 或 119 比較快。
【表】一些緊急電話號碼（112 的年份是正式選定的年份）：號碼、開始的地區、開始年份、目前可接通的服務。

open_tasks.prompt: A friend from another country is visiting Taiwan and asks which number to call in an emergency. Based on the passage, give your friend advice in 1–2 English sentences and explain why.
reference_answers: Call 119 for a fire or an ambulance and 110 for the police, because these numbers connect you directly; use 112 only if your phone has no SIM card or a weak signal.
If you can, dial 110 or 119 directly, since 112 first plays a recorded message; but if your phone has no SIM card, 112 still works, and you press 9 for fire or ambulance help.
